subject: Civil Engineering
title: Waterproofing: Keeping Tunnels Dry
description: One-minute skill: Waterproofing: Keeping Tunnels Dry.

hook.text: Every tunnel leaks. The question is how much — and whether the system can handle it.

buildup.text: PVC membranes wrap the tunnel between the initial and final linings — a waterproof sandwich.

discovery.text: Drained systems accept some water and channel it to sumps — pumps remove it continuously.

twist.text: Tanked systems block all water — needed for rail tunnels where any moisture on tracks is unsafe.

climax.text: The Channel Tunnel pumps 72 million liters of water per day — leakage is constant.

punchline.text: No tunnel is perfectly dry. Managing water is a permanent job underground.

quiz.question: How much water does the Channel Tunnel pump out daily?

details.summary: Tunnel waterproofing systems prevent groundwater from entering the tunnel interior using combinations of watertight lining, membrane sheets, injection grouting, and drainage systems.
details.whyItMatters: Water infiltration damages tunnel finishes, corrodes reinforcement, creates safety hazards, and increases maintenance costs dramatically. Effective waterproofing extends tunnel service life to over one hundred years.
takeaways: Tanked systems seal the tunnel completely with waterproof membranes or linings
Drained systems collect and channel groundwater to pumping stations
Injection grouting seals water-bearing fractures in the surrounding rock mass

faq.question: What is the difference between tanked and drained waterproofing approaches?
faq.answer: Tanked systems seal water out completely using continuous membranes or watertight structural concrete, accepting full hydrostatic pressure on the lining. Drained systems relieve pressure by collecting water behind the lining and channeling it to sumps.

faq.question: How do waterproof membranes work in tunnel construction?
faq.answer: PVC or polyolefin sheets are installed between the initial shotcrete lining and the final cast-in-place concrete lining. Sheets are heat-welded at seams. Fleece backing material protects the membrane from damage. This creates a continuous waterproof barrier around the entire tunnel circumference.
